outlook.statement: Invest further in technology, strengthen digital capabilities, expand regional and multilingual reach, extract greater value from content portfolio, deepen relationships with audiences and advertisers, stay disciplined in capital allocation and focused on operational excellence to create sustainable long-term value
Technology will keep reshaping the media landscape; protecting and compounding trust remains highest priority

Connected TV is rapidly approaching the USD 1 billion advertising market in 2026, and the Company's CTV footprint, multiple digital platforms, and engaging content archive monetisation position it to capture a wider audience in the coming time.
Live events remained the highest-growing segment in the Indian Media & Entertainment industry with 43.6% Y-o-Y growth, even ahead of Digital Media.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) projects the Indian economic growth at 6.9% in FY27, driven by resilient domestic demand, continued expansion in the services and manufacturing sectors, rising capital formation, growth in service exports and an improving external environment.
Digital advertising revenue seen growing at a CAGR of 9.2% through 2030 with USD 26.5 billion, from USD 18.8 billion in 2026, led by growth in connected TV, retail media, and performance marketing.

ZMCL's long-term strategy centres on developing an integrated media ecosystem where television, digital publishing, mobile applications, social platforms and experiential properties operate as complementary audience touchpoints.
The Company continues to diversify revenue beyond conventional advertising and subscription income by unlocking the value of its extensive content library and proprietary brand and content IPs.

Investment in technology is a strategic priority; the Company continues to strengthen capabilities through ongoing investments in technology infrastructure, platform development and specialized talent.
New initiatives evaluated through rigorous framework with measurable milestones, performance reviews, contingency plans, and disciplined go/no-go decision frameworks.

Going forward, the Group will continue to focus on improving operational cash flows through revenue growth, cost optimisation, diversification of revenue streams and planned capital infusion. These measures are expected to strengthen the Company's financial position, support the settlement of liabilities and provide the necessary resources to sustain and grow its business operations.
The Indian media and entertainment sector is expected to grow at 8% in 2026 and reach Rs 3.3 trillion by 2028.
Global Entertainment & Media industry anticipated to grow at a CAGR of 3.4% and reach USD 4.2 trillion by 2030.

The Board approved incorporation of a WOS in India to engage in the business of bringing forth ancient knowledge of scriptures intersecting with modern science, focusing on spirituality, mindfulness and wellbeing through the launch of appropriate digital and alternative media properties in the infotainment space.

Board of Director's approved business plan for the next financial year, capital infusion in addition to the monetization through new revenue streams and cost rationalisation measures along with other measures taken by the Company

The Company has been proactively exploring and executing new, sustainable revenue streams, including the conceptualisation of new brand and Intellectual Properties (IPs) and the monetisation of its content archives.
The Company's business plan for the next financial year, as approved by the Board of Directors, exhibits plans to secure higher revenues thereby further improving operational cash flows.

Market Competition Risk: Highly competitive Indian news media landscape with established national/regional brands and proliferating state/local operators; availability of free news content intensifies competition.
Technology Risk: Rapid evolution of AI, connected TV, OTT streaming, broadband infrastructure challenging existing business models; pace of digital change can outstrip implementation speed.
Variability in Advertising Revenue Risk: Advertising revenues susceptible to economic conditions, advertiser sentiment, consumer demand, competitive pressures.
Intellectual Property Rights Risk: Unauthorized use or adverse legal outcomes affecting IP could impact commercial value, revenue generation, brand reputation.
Feasibility Risk of New Initiatives: Execution risk from new platforms, products, business models; outcomes may be affected by competitive responses and external factors.
Macro-level Risk: Geopolitical developments, public policy changes, social/consumer trends, macroeconomic conditions influencing consumer spending and advertising budgets.

Litigation Risk: Editorial accuracy, objectivity, credibility, responsible journalism fundamental; inaccurate reporting or non-compliance may expose to legal proceedings, regulatory action, reputational damage.
Manpower Risk: Intense competition for key executives, senior journalists, technical professionals, digital media specialists, leadership talent.

Regulatory Risk: Highly regulated environment governed by MIB, TRAI, SEBI, MCA, Income Tax Authorities; changes may influence content distribution, censorship, compliance, tax liabilities, operational burdens.

MSMEs contributed ₹358 billion (38% of digital advertising spend), Q-commerce advertising surged 202% YoY to ₹40 billion
Online news traffic declined by 9% in 2025 as AI-generated search summaries reduced direct referrals
YouTube (55%) and WhatsApp (46%) emerged as leading news consumption platforms
Digital news monetisation remained constrained with subscription revenues of ₹5 billion (just 3% of print advertising revenues)
Zee Media Network reached 212 million average monthly viewers across linear TV network in FY26.
Websites registered average monthly 91.2 million users; apps recorded 7.97 million monthly average users and 13.55 million downloads during FY26.
Collective social media reach of 1.05 billion on Facebook, Instagram, X, and YouTube.
Employee composition: 79% men, 21% women; 77% permanent, 23% contractual/temporary.
Tenure-based composition: 24% (0-2 years), 50% (3-5 years), 13% (6-10 years), 13% (above 10 years).
Consolidated Revenue from Operations grew 22.07% to Rs 7,591.75 million in FY26 from Rs 6,219.15 million in FY25.
Revenue composition FY26: 78% advertising, 5% subscription, 17% content archive licensing.
Content archive licensing monetized Rs 1,320.39 million in FY26 vs Rs 4.25 million in FY25.
Consolidated Profit after tax: Rs 18.92 million in FY26 vs loss of Rs 1,194.15 million in FY25.
Standalone Profit after tax: Rs 169.23 million in FY26 vs loss of Rs 1,003.46 million in FY25.
Company met all debt and interest servicing obligations during FY26.
